findings.headline: In‑race stress stayed low through wet‑dry transition
findings.detail: The driver’s stress spiked to 17.3 only after the race, confirming that in‑race stress remained low despite the wet‑to‑dry transition; no in‑race stress data exceed 10, so the driver handled the changing conditions without physiological strain.

findings.headline: Wet surface caused major pace loss, tyres not at fault
findings.detail: Pace dropped sharply (+8.351 s) on lap 19 when the track went wet, but the modelled tyre degradation on the medium tyres stayed low (+0.177 s/lap) indicating the slowdown was surface‑driven, not tyre‑related; the driver should focus on tyre choice rather than tyre wear for wet periods.
evidence: modelled deg +0.177 s/lap for medium stint 1‑26

findings.headline: Intermediates restored pace but began degrading as track cooled
findings.detail: After switching to intermediates (lap 27) the driver’s pace delta fell back to near‑zero despite the track remaining wet, showing the tyre change recovered lost time; however, a slight +0.353 s on lap 33 suggests the intermediate set began to lose grip as the track cooled to 20.7 °C.

findings.headline: Softs lost time when rain returned on lap 45
findings.detail: The soft tyre stint (lap 38‑51) delivered a best lap of 91.277 s and a negative modelled degradation (‑0.224 s/lap), yet pace rose again (+1.728 s) on lap 45 when rain returned, indicating the softs were vulnerable to sudden wet patches; consider delaying soft deployment until after lap 45 or preparing a quicker intermediate swap.
evidence: modelled deg -0.224 s/lap for soft stint

findings.headline: No pace loss while lapping backmarkers under blue flags
findings.detail: Blue flags appeared from lap 21 onward while the driver was on medium tyres; despite the extra traffic the pace delta stayed at 0 s on laps 21‑25, suggesting the driver managed backmarkers without losing time, but the lack of stress data means confidence is limited.

findings.headline: Minor pace rise on lap 41 under blue flag, stress unknown
findings.detail: A small pace increase (+0.371 s) on lap 41 occurred on soft tyres under dry conditions with a blue flag, but the driver’s stress reading is unavailable; with only one data point the pattern is uncertain, so monitor for possible concentration dips on similar laps.
